usage: The most common praise: “well done”, “good job”. Said to children and adults alike — for effort and for a good result. You can add a name: “Tubli, Mari!”.
examples: Oled tubli! — You’re doing great! • Tubli, et sa iga päev harjutad. — Well done for practising every day.

usage: A stronger “tubli”: väga means “very”. Praise for hard work or an excellent result.
examples: Väga tubli, kõik vastused on õiged! — Very well done, all the answers are correct! • Te olete väga tublid! — You’ve all done really well!
reply: Aitäh, sina ka! — Thanks, you too!

usage: Literally “well done”. Praise for a specific result: a piece of work, a task, a solution.
examples: Hästi tehtud, poisid! — Nicely done, guys! • Ülesanne on hästi tehtud. — The task has been done well.

usage: “Good job!” — often said to colleagues, a team or athletes.
examples: Hea töö, meeskond! — Good job, team! • See oli tõesti hea töö. — That was really good work.
reply: Aitäh, rõõm kuulda! — Thanks, glad to hear it!

usage: From hakkama saama — “to manage, to cope”. Said when something difficult has worked out.
examples: Said hakkama, palju õnne! — You did it, congratulations! • Me saime hakkama! — We did it!
reply: Jah, sain hakkama! — Yes, I did it!

usage: “Excellent!”, “superb!” — strong and slightly formal praise.
examples: Suurepärane tulemus! — An excellent result! • Sinu eesti keel on suurepärane. — Your Estonian is excellent.

usage: A simple assessment, like at school: “very good”.
examples: Väga hea, jätka! — Very good, keep going! • Väga hea vastus. — A very good answer.

usage: “Great!”, “lovely!” — joy about good news or a good result. A very common word.
examples: Tore, et sa tulid! — Great that you came! • Kõik õige? Tore! — All correct? Great!
reply: Mul on ka hea meel! — I’m glad too!

usage: Praise and a wish to keep going at the same pace. Formal or to several people: “Jätkake samas vaimus!”.
examples: Hästi läheb, jätka samas vaimus! — It’s going well, keep up the good work! • Jätkake samas vaimus! — Keep up the good work! (to several people)

usage: Approval when everything is done right: “exactly”, “that’s it”.
examples: Just nii, väga hea! — Exactly, very good! • Just nii tulebki seda teha. — That’s exactly how it should be done.

usage: Colloquial. A tegija is someone who gets things done — a real pro.
examples: Sa oled ikka tegija! — You really are a star! • Ta on oma alal tõeline tegija. — He’s a real pro in his field.
reply: Aitäh, sina ka! — Thanks, you too!

usage: Colloquial: said when something is impressive.
examples: Vägev, kõik õige! — Awesome, all correct! • See oli vägev elamus. — That was an amazing experience.

usage: Colloquial: “cool”, “nice”. A very common word.
examples: Lahe, et sul õnnestus! — Cool that it worked out for you! • Väga lahe pidu! — A really cool party!

usage: Colloquial: “awesome”, “fire” — admiration. Even stronger: “Üliäge!”.
examples: Äge tunne on! — It’s an awesome feeling! • Oi, kui äge! — Wow, how awesome!

usage: Colloquial: “brilliant”, “great”. Close to “äge” and “lahe”.
examples: Täitsa vinge! — Totally brilliant! • Oli alles vinge päev! — What a brilliant day it was!

usage: Just like in English: “Super!”. Fits almost any situation.
examples: Super, kõik vastused on õiged! — Super, all the answers are correct! • See on super idee. — That’s a super idea.

usage: Like at the theatre: admiration and applause.
examples: Braavo, väga hea! — Bravo, very good! • Braavo, sa tegid selle ära! — Bravo, you did it!

usage: When the result is truly big: “powerful”, “impressive”.
examples: Võimas tulemus! — An impressive result! • Kakskümmend õiget vastust järjest, võimas! — Twenty correct answers in a row, impressive!

usage: Warm, slightly enthusiastic praise: “wonderful”, “marvellous”.
examples: Imeline, et sa iga päev õpid! — It’s wonderful that you study every day! • Imeline päev! — A wonderful day!

usage: An exclamation of joy, like “Yes!” or “Hooray!”. Said about your own success.
examples: Jess, sain hakkama! — Yes, I did it! • Jess, täna on reede! — Yay, it’s Friday!
